subject: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah@finbot.ai>, Tom Rivas <tom@finbot.ai>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:20:00 -0000
Subject: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps. Let me know if I missed anything.

1) High-level pain / goal
- Primary pain: inference unit economics — per-request token cost is currently squeezing margins on FinBot's realtime features (notably summarization and personalization).
- Goal: reduce per-request cost while keeping P95 latency under 300ms for the 99th percentile of web requests, and preserve output quality for short-form summarization and billing notes.

2) Current stack
- Inference: in-house endpoints on GCP (n1-standard + T4) for prod; batch/async on-prem for nightly jobs.
- Model: mixture of open LLMs (Llama-variant for cost-sensitive endpoints) and a small proprietary finetune.
- Observability: basic request logs + token counts; no unified cost attribution per route today.

3) Cost levers we discussed (notes from call)
- Batching: average batch size today ~1.4; opportunity to increase via client-side micro-batching for some routes.
- Caching: prefix caching for repeated prompts could be high impact for summarization templates.
- Quantization: you said you are open to int8 / 4-bit quantized models for non-sensitive routes; need to confirm acceptable quality delta.

4) Success criteria / metrics
- 30-40% reduction in per-token inference cost (or per-request cost) for targeted routes within 90 days of deployment.
- Maintain/Improve quality as measured by the existing summarization eval set (no more than 5% quality regression by internal metrics).
- P95 latency <300ms for interactive endpoints under expected load.

5) Risks / constraints
- Some prompts touch sensitive PII; these will need dedicated routing (private deployment or dedicated capacity) and different quantization/caching policies.
- Procurement window: you mentioned procurement review in early April.

6) Next steps
- I'll send a one-page discovery recap (attached) with the three configurations we discussed: Hosted (with caching + batching), Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private w/ HSM for sensitive routes.
- Dylan/Evelyn will put together a back-of-envelope cost comparison (per-token) for int8 vs baseline FP16 and expected latency impact.
- Sarah/Tom: confirm the procurement contact (Procurement email copied) and your preferred pilot start date (you mentioned mid-March as possible).

Attachment: RWI-Discovery-Recap.pdf (PDF, 85KB) — includes quick config pricing and expected tradeoffs.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Sarah Kim <sarah@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Rivas <tom@finbot.ai>, procurement@finbot.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 18:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few clarifications inline: 

> Primary pain: inference unit economics — per-request token cost is currently squeezing margins on FinBot's realtime features.

Yes — exactly. Our summaries run on every user session; small improvements in unit cost compound quickly.

> Batching: average batch size today ~1.4; opportunity to increase via client-side micro-batching for some routes.

Correct on the 1.4 average. We can likely introduce a small buffer on non-critical routes to increase batching to ~3–4. Latency tradeoffs acceptable for async/background features but not for the live composer.

> Quantization: you said you are open to int8 / 4-bit quantized models for non-sensitive routes; need to confirm acceptable quality delta.

We are open to trying int8 for the summary route; we require an A/B eval on 1k representative prompts to validate quality. If degradation >5% against our scoring, we can't move forward for that route.

Procurement: procurement@finbot.ai is the right contact for now. My target is to get internal approval by the second week of April.

Thanks again — can you and Dylan share the cost vs quality matrix you mentioned? If possible, include an estimated cost per 1M tokens for each config (hosted + caching, dedicated + quantized, private).

Best,
Sarah
Head of Platform Engineering | FinBot
sarah@finbot.ai

Sarah / Tom — short follow-up and proposed timeline based on internal readiness: 

Proposed pilot (2–4 week):
- Scope: Summary route only (non-PII traffic).
- Configs to test:
  1) Hosted + caching + request-side micro-batching (target batch 3): measure cost delta and p95 latency.
  2) Hosted + int8 quantization (no caching) — measure quality delta on 1k prompts.
  3) Dedicated reserved capacity + int8 (if pilot shows cost/latency wins).

Deliverables (what we'll provide):
- Cost estimates: per-1M-token for each config (Dylan)
- Quality A/B on 1k prompts for int8 vs baseline (Evelyn)
- Implementation plan & rollbacks (Marissa)

Timeline:
- Mon (Mar 2): Dylan uploads cost spreadsheet + quick slides to shared Drive.
- Tue (Mar 3)–Thu (Mar 5): Evelyn runs the 1k prompt eval; shares results.
- Mon (Mar 9): Align on final pilot config; procurement kickoff soon after.

Action items for FinBot:
- Confirm pilot start (mid-Mar ok?) and the procurement owner (procurement@finbot.ai copied).
- Share the 1k prompt set or approve Redwood to sample from production (we prefer a Sanboxed sample).

If that timeline looks good, I'll schedule a 30-minute alignment call next week to finalize the pilot config.
